title: Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems and Organizations

source.notes: Generated from NIST OSCAL JSON. Includes 800-53 Rev 5 cross-references via OSCAL link resolution.

03.01.01.title: Account Management
03.01.01.description: Define the types of system accounts allowed and prohibited. Create, enable, modify, disable, and remove system accounts in accordance with policy, procedures, prerequisites, and criteria. Specify: Authorized users of the system, Group and role membership, and Access authorizations (i.e., privileges) for each account. Authorize access to the system based on: A valid access authorization and Intended system usage. Monitor the use of system accounts. Disable system accounts when: The accounts have expired, The accounts have been inactive for [time period], The accounts are no longer associated with a user or individual, The accounts are in violation of organizational policy, or Significant risks associated with individuals are discovered. Notify account managers and designated personnel or roles within: [time period] when accounts are no longer required. [time period] when users are terminated or transferred. [time period] when system usage or the need-to-know changes for an individual. Require that users log out of the system after [time period] of expected inactivity or when [circumstances].

03.01.04.title: Separation of Duties
03.01.04.description: Identify the duties of individuals requiring separation. Define system access authorizations to support separation of duties.

03.01.05.title: Least Privilege
03.01.05.description: Allow only authorized system access for users (or processes acting on behalf of users) that is necessary to accomplish assigned organizational tasks. Authorize access to [security functions] and [security-relevant information]. Review the privileges assigned to roles or classes of users [frequency] to validate the need for such privileges. Reassign or remove privileges, as necessary.

03.01.06.title: Least Privilege – Privileged Accounts
03.01.06.description: Restrict privileged accounts on the system to [personnel or roles].. Require that users (or roles) with privileged accounts use non-privileged accounts when accessing non-security functions or non-security information.

03.01.07.title: Least Privilege – Privileged Functions
03.01.07.description: Prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions. Log the execution of privileged functions.

03.01.08.title: Unsuccessful Logon Attempts
03.01.08.description: Enforce a limit of [number] consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a [time period]. Automatically [SELECTED PARAMETER VALUES] when the maximum number of unsuccessful attempts is exceeded.

03.01.10.title: Device Lock
03.01.10.description: Prevent access to the system by [SELECTED PARAMETER VALUES]. Retain the device lock until the user reestablishes access using established identification and authentication procedures. Conceal, via the device lock, information previously visible on the display with a publicly viewable image.

03.01.12.title: Remote Access
03.01.12.description: Establish usage restrictions, configuration requirements, and connection requirements for each type of allowable remote system access. Authorize each type of remote system access prior to establishing such connections. Route remote access to the system through authorized and managed access control points. Authorize the remote execution of privileged commands and remote access to security-relevant information.

03.01.16.title: Wireless Access
03.01.16.description: Establish usage restrictions, configuration requirements, and connection requirements for each type of wireless access to the system. Authorize each type of wireless access to the system prior to establishing such connections. Disable, when not intended for use, wireless networking capabilities prior to issuance and deployment. Protect wireless access to the system using authentication and encryption.

03.01.18.title: Access Control for Mobile Devices
03.01.18.description: Establish usage restrictions, configuration requirements, and connection requirements for mobile devices. Authorize the connection of mobile devices to the system. Implement full-device or container-based encryption to protect the confidentiality of CUI on mobile devices.

03.01.20.title: Use of External Systems
03.01.20.description: Prohibit the use of external systems unless the systems are specifically authorized. Establish the following security requirements to be satisfied on external systems prior to allowing use of or access to those systems by authorized individuals: [security requirements]. Permit authorized individuals to use external systems to access the organizational system or to process, store, or transmit CUI only after: Verifying that the security requirements on the external systems as specified in the organization’s system security plans have been satisfied and Retaining approved system connection or processing agreements with the organizational entities hosting the external systems. Restrict the use of organization-controlled portable storage devices by authorized individuals on external systems.

03.01.22.title: Publicly Accessible Content
03.01.22.description: Train authorized individuals to ensure that publicly accessible information does not contain CUI. Review the content on publicly accessible systems for CUI and remove such information, if discovered.

03.02.01.title: Literacy Training and Awareness
03.02.01.description: Provide security literacy training to system users: As part of initial training for new users and [frequency] thereafter, When required by system changes or following [events], and On recognizing and reporting indicators of insider threat, social engineering, and social mining. Update security literacy training content [frequency] and following [events].

03.02.02.title: Role-Based Training
03.02.02.description: Provide role-based security training to organizational personnel: Before authorizing access to the system or CUI, before performing assigned duties, and [frequency] thereafter When required by system changes or following [events]. Update role-based training content [frequency] and following [events].

03.03.01.title: Event Logging
03.03.01.description: Specify the following event types selected for logging within the system: [event types]. Review and update the event types selected for logging [frequency].

03.03.02.title: Audit Record Content
03.03.02.description: Include the following content in audit records: What type of event occurred When the event occurred Where the event occurred Source of the event Outcome of the event Identity of the individuals, subjects, objects, or entities associated with the event Provide additional information for audit records as needed.

03.03.03.title: Audit Record Generation
03.03.03.description: Generate audit records for the selected event types and audit record content specified in 03.03.01 and 03.03.02. Retain audit records for a time period consistent with the records retention policy.

03.03.04.title: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
03.03.04.description: Alert organizational personnel or roles within [time period] in the event of an audit logging process failure. Take the following additional actions: [additional actions].

03.03.05.title: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
03.03.05.description: Review and analyze system audit records [frequency] for indications and the potential impact of inappropriate or unusual activity. Report findings to organizational personnel or roles. Analyze and correlate audit records across different repositories to gain organization-wide situational awareness.

03.03.06.title: Audit Record Reduction and Report Generation
03.03.06.description: Implement an audit record reduction and report generation capability that supports audit record review, analysis, reporting requirements, and after-the-fact investigations of incidents. Preserve the original content and time ordering of audit records.

03.03.07.title: Time Stamps
03.03.07.description: Use internal system clocks to generate time stamps for audit records. Record time stamps for audit records that meet [granularity of time measurement] and that use Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), have a fixed local time offset from UTC, or include the local time offset as part of the time stamp.

03.03.08.title: Protection of Audit Information
03.03.08.description: Protect audit information and audit logging tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion. Authorize access to management of audit logging functionality to only a subset of privileged users or roles.

03.04.01.title: Baseline Configuration
03.04.01.description: Develop and maintain under configuration control, a current baseline configuration of the system. Review and update the baseline configuration of the system [frequency] and when system components are installed or modified.

03.04.02.title: Configuration Settings
03.04.02.description: Establish, document, and implement the following configuration settings for the system that reflect the most restrictive mode consistent with operational requirements: [configuration settings] . Identify, document, and approve any deviations from established configuration settings.

03.04.03.title: Configuration Change Control
03.04.03.description: Define the types of changes to the system that are configuration-controlled. Review proposed configuration-controlled changes to the system, and approve or disapprove such changes with explicit consideration for security impacts. Implement and document approved configuration-controlled changes to the system. Monitor and review activities associated with configuration-controlled changes to the system.

03.04.04.title: Impact Analyses
03.04.04.description: Analyze changes to the system to determine potential security impacts prior to change implementation. Verify that the security requirements for the system continue to be satisfied after the system changes have been implemented.

03.04.06.title: Least Functionality
03.04.06.description: Configure the system to provide only mission-essential capabilities. Prohibit or restrict use of the following functions, ports, protocols, connections, and services: [functions] . Review the system [frequency] to identify unnecessary or nonsecure functions, ports, protocols, connections, and services. Disable or remove functions, ports, protocols, connections, and services that are unnecessary or nonsecure.

03.04.08.title: Authorized Software – Allow by Exception
03.04.08.description: Identify software programs authorized to execute on the system. Implement a deny-all, allow-by-exception policy for the execution of authorized software programs on the system. Review and update the list of authorized software programs [frequency].

03.04.10.title: System Component Inventory
03.04.10.description: Develop and document an inventory of system components. Review and update the system component inventory [frequency]. Update the system component inventory as part of installations, removals, and system updates.

03.04.11.title: Information Location
03.04.11.description: Identify and document the location of CUI and the system components on which the information is processed and stored. Document changes to the system or system component location where CUI is processed and stored.

03.04.12.title: System and Component Configuration for High-Risk Areas
03.04.12.description: Issue systems or system components with the following configurations to individuals traveling to high-risk locations: [configurations]. Apply the following security requirements to the systems or components when the individuals return from travel: [security requirements].

03.05.01.title: User Identification and Authentication
03.05.01.description: Uniquely identify and authenticate system users, and associate that unique identification with processes acting on behalf of those users. Re-authenticate users when [circumstances or situations] .

03.05.05.title: Identifier Management
03.05.05.description: Receive authorization from organizational personnel or roles to assign an individual, group, role, service, or device identifier. Select and assign an identifier that identifies an individual, group, role, service, or device. Prevent the reuse of identifiers for [time period]. Manage individual identifiers by uniquely identifying each individual as [characteristic].

03.05.07.title: Password Management
03.05.07.description: Maintain a list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords, and update the list [frequency] and when organizational passwords are suspected to have been compromised. Verify that passwords are not found on the list of commonly used, expected, or compromised passwords when users create or update passwords. Transmit passwords only over cryptographically protected channels. Store passwords in a cryptographically protected form. Select a new password upon first use after account recovery. Enforce the following composition and complexity rules for passwords: [rules].

03.05.12.title: Authenticator Management
03.05.12.description: Verify the identity of the individual, group, role, service, or device receiving the authenticator as part of the initial authenticator distribution. Establish initial authenticator content for any authenticators issued by the organization. Establish and implement administrative procedures for initial authenticator distribution; for lost, compromised, or damaged authenticators; and for revoking authenticators. Change default authenticators at first use. Change or refresh authenticators [frequency] or when the following events occur: [events]. Protect authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification.

03.06.02.title: Incident Monitoring, Reporting, and Response Assistance
03.06.02.description: Track and document system security incidents. Report suspected incidents to the organizational incident response capability within [time period]. Report incident information to [authorities]. Provide an incident response support resource that offers advice and assistance to system users on handling and reporting incidents.

03.06.04.title: Incident Response Training
03.06.04.description: Provide incident response training to system users consistent with assigned roles and responsibilities: Within [time period] of assuming an incident response role or responsibility or acquiring system access, When required by system changes, and [frequency] thereafter. Review and update incident response training content [frequency] and following [events].

03.06.05.title: Incident Response Plan
03.06.05.description: Develop an incident response plan that: Provides the organization with a roadmap for implementing its incident response capability, Describes the structure and organization of the incident response capability, Provides a high-level approach for how the incident response capability fits into the overall organization, Defines reportable incidents, Addresses the sharing of incident information, and Designates responsibilities to organizational entities, personnel, or roles. Distribute copies of the incident response plan to designated incident response personnel (identified by name and/or by role) and organizational elements. Update the incident response plan to address system and organizational changes or problems encountered during plan implementation, execution, or testing. Protect the incident response plan from unauthorized disclosure.

03.07.04.title: Maintenance Tools
03.07.04.description: Approve, control, and monitor the use of system maintenance tools. Check media with diagnostic and test programs for malicious code before it is used in the system. Prevent the removal of system maintenance equipment containing CUI by verifying that there is no CUI on the equipment, sanitizing or destroying the equipment, or retaining the equipment within the facility.

03.07.05.title: Nonlocal Maintenance
03.07.05.description: Approve and monitor nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic activities. Implement multi-factor authentication and replay resistance in the establishment of nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic sessions. Terminate session and network connections when nonlocal maintenance is completed.

03.07.06.title: Maintenance Personnel
03.07.06.description: Establish a process for maintenance personnel authorization. Maintain a list of authorized maintenance organizations or personnel. Verify that non-escorted personnel who perform maintenance on the system possess the required access authorizations. Designate organizational personnel with required access authorizations and technical competence to supervise the maintenance activities of personnel who do not possess the required access authorizations.

03.08.05.title: Media Transport
03.08.05.description: Protect and control system media that contain CUI during transport outside of controlled areas. Maintain accountability of system media that contain CUI during transport outside of controlled areas. Document activities associated with the transport of system media that contain CUI.

03.08.07.title: Media Use
03.08.07.description: Restrict or prohibit the use of [types of system media]. Prohibit the use of removable system media without an identifiable owner.

03.08.09.title: System Backup – Cryptographic Protection
03.08.09.description: Protect the confidentiality of backup information. Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent the unauthorized disclosure of CUI at backup storage locations.

03.09.01.title: Personnel Screening
03.09.01.description: Screen individuals prior to authorizing access to the system. Rescreen individuals in accordance with [conditions].

03.09.02.title: Personnel Termination and Transfer
03.09.02.description: When individual employment is terminated: Disable system access within [time period], Terminate or revoke authenticators and credentials associated with the individual, and Retrieve security-related system property. When individuals are reassigned or transferred to other positions in the organization: Review and confirm the ongoing operational need for current logical and physical access authorizations to the system and facility, and Modify access authorization to correspond with any changes in operational need.

03.10.01.title: Physical Access Authorizations
03.10.01.description: Develop, approve, and maintain a list of individuals with authorized access to the facility where the system resides. Issue authorization credentials for facility access. Review the facility access list [frequency]. Remove individuals from the facility access list when access is no longer required.

03.10.02.title: Monitoring Physical Access
03.10.02.description: Monitor physical access to the facility where the system resides to detect and respond to physical security incidents. Review physical access logs [frequency] and upon occurrence of [events or potential indicators of events].

03.10.06.title: Alternate Work Site
03.10.06.description: Determine alternate work sites allowed for use by employees. Employ the following security requirements at alternate work sites: [security requirements].

03.10.07.title: Physical Access Control
03.10.07.description: Enforce physical access authorizations at entry and exit points to the facility where the system resides by: Verifying individual physical access authorizations before granting access to the facility and Controlling ingress and egress with physical access control systems, devices, or guards. Maintain physical access audit logs for entry or exit points. Escort visitors, and control visitor activity. Secure keys, combinations, and other physical access devices. Control physical access to output devices to prevent unauthorized individuals from obtaining access to CUI.

03.11.01.title: Risk Assessment
03.11.01.description: Assess the risk (including supply chain risk) of unauthorized disclosure resulting from the processing, storage, or transmission of CUI. Update risk assessments [frequency].

03.11.02.title: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
03.11.02.description: Monitor and scan the system for vulnerabilities [frequency] and when new vulnerabilities affecting the system are identified. Remediate system vulnerabilities within [response times]. Update system vulnerabilities to be scanned [frequency] and when new vulnerabilities are identified and reported.

03.12.02.title: Plan of Action and Milestones
03.12.02.description: Develop a plan of action and milestones for the system: To document the planned remediation actions to correct weaknesses or deficiencies noted during security assessments and To reduce or eliminate known system vulnerabilities. Update the existing plan of action and milestones based on the findings from: Security assessments, Audits or reviews, and Continuous monitoring activities.

03.12.05.title: Information Exchange
03.12.05.description: Approve and manage the exchange of CUI between the system and other systems using [SELECTED PARAMETER VALUES]. Document interface characteristics, security requirements, and responsibilities for each system as part of the exchange agreements. Review and update the exchange agreements [frequency].

03.13.01.title: Boundary Protection
03.13.01.description: Monitor and control communications at external managed interfaces to the system and key internal managed interfaces within the system. Implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are physically or logically separated from internal networks. Connect to external systems only through managed interfaces that consist of boundary protection devices arranged in accordance with an organizational security architecture.

03.13.06.title: Network Communications – Deny by Default – Allow by Exception
03.13.06.description: Network Communications – Deny by Default – Allow by Exception

03.13.12.title: Collaborative Computing Devices and Applications
03.13.12.description: Prohibit the remote activation of collaborative computing devices and applications with the following exceptions: [exceptions]. Provide an explicit indication of use to users physically present at the devices.

03.13.13.title: Mobile Code
03.13.13.description: Define acceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies. Authorize, monitor, and control the use of mobile code.

03.14.01.title: Flaw Remediation
03.14.01.description: Identify, report, and correct system flaws. Install security-relevant software and firmware updates within [time period] of the release of the updates.

03.14.02.title: Malicious Code Protection
03.14.02.description: Implement malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code. Update malicious code protection mechanisms as new releases are available in accordance with configuration management policies and procedures. Configure malicious code protection mechanisms to: Perform scans of the system [frequency] and real-time scans of files from external sources at endpoints or system entry and exit points as the files are downloaded, opened, or executed; and Block malicious code, quarantine malicious code, or take other mitigation actions in response to malicious code detection.

03.14.03.title: Security Alerts, Advisories, and Directives
03.14.03.description: Receive system security alerts, advisories, and directives from external organizations on an ongoing basis. Generate and disseminate internal system security alerts, advisories, and directives, as necessary.

03.14.06.title: System Monitoring
03.14.06.description: Monitor the system to detect: Attacks and indicators of potential attacks and Unauthorized connections. Identify unauthorized use of the system. Monitor inbound and outbound communications traffic to detect unusual or unauthorized activities or conditions.

03.15.01.title: Policy and Procedures
03.15.01.description: Develop, document, and disseminate to organizational personnel or roles the policies and procedures needed to satisfy the security requirements for the protection of CUI. Review and update policies and procedures [frequency].

03.15.02.title: System Security Plan
03.15.02.description: Develop a system security plan that: Defines the constituent system components; Identifies the information types processed, stored, and transmitted by the system; Describes specific threats to the system that are of concern to the organization; Describes the operational environment for the system and any dependencies on or connections to other systems or system components; Provides an overview of the security requirements for the system; Describes the safeguards in place or planned for meeting the security requirements; Identifies individuals that fulfill system roles and responsibilities; and Includes other relevant information necessary for the protection of CUI. Review and update the system security plan [frequency]. Protect the system security plan from unauthorized disclosure.

03.15.03.title: Rules of Behavior
03.15.03.description: Establish rules that describe the responsibilities and expected behavior for system usage and protecting CUI. Provide rules to individuals who require access to the system. Receive a documented acknowledgement from individuals indicating that they have read, understand, and agree to abide by the rules of behavior before authorizing access to CUI and the system. Review and update the rules of behavior [frequency].

03.16.02.title: Unsupported System Components
03.16.02.description: Replace system components when support for the components is no longer available from the developer, vendor, or manufacturer. Provide options for risk mitigation or alternative sources for continued support for unsupported components that cannot be replaced.

03.16.03.title: External System Services
03.16.03.description: Require the providers of external system services used for the processing, storage, or transmission of CUI to comply with the following security requirements: [security requirements]. Define and document user roles and responsibilities with regard to external system services, including shared responsibilities with external service providers. Implement processes, methods, and techniques to monitor security requirement compliance by external service providers on an ongoing basis.

03.17.01.title: Supply Chain Risk Management Plan
03.17.01.description: Develop a plan for managing supply chain risks associated with the research and development, design, manufacturing, acquisition, delivery, integration, operations, maintenance, and disposal of the system, system components, or system services. Review and update the supply chain risk management plan [frequency]. Protect the supply chain risk management plan from unauthorized disclosure.

03.17.03.title: Supply Chain Requirements and Processes
03.17.03.description: Establish a process for identifying and addressing weaknesses or deficiencies in the supply chain elements and processes. Enforce the following security requirements to protect against supply chain risks to the system, system components, or system services and to limit the harm or consequences from supply chain-related events: [security requirements].
